common_concerns: Whether fitting electronic entry hardware means permanently drilling the existing front door — the Word of Mouth review of Precision Locksmiths (Spotswood) records a local job where the front door had to be "core drilled (a small 5mm hole drilled right through the core of the door)", while smartdoorlocks.com.au's retrofit guidance is explicitly about choosing a smart mortise lock "to minimise alternations to the door", so the irreversibility of the door modification is a live question for this suburb.

Whether the smart lock will tie into an alarm or existing security system rather than replace it — the same Spotswood review describes the core drilling being done "to install an electronic door strike for the alarm system", evidencing that local buyers arrive with an alarm already installed and expect the new entry hardware to integrate with it.

Whether an existing security or screen door in front of the main door blocks the smart lock — smartlockinstallation.com.au/service requires customers to supply the "Distance with security door (if any) and height of both current door handles" before it will quote, so a second outer door is a known Australian install blocker (national record; not Spotswood-verified).

Whether the installer actually handles the brand the customer has already bought — smartlockinstallation.com.au names 27 brands it installs (Bosch, Philips, Aqara, Kaadas, Klug, Lenovo, Sharp, Solity, Eufy, Samsung, August, Yale, Lockwood, Schlage, Lockly, Lemaar, Lane, Kwikset, Xiaomi, Kogan, Orion, AusLock, SDL, DDL, Moorgen, Ezviz, McGrath) and Lockwood's own page splits its SDL Smart Leverset across "New installation/Retrofitting", evidencing a fragmented market where brand-and-door fit is a live question (national records; not Spotswood-verified).
